_note: Criteria judged from the reference list after the citation check (V-098). A criterion matches a strategy by its own level descriptors, never by its name: at least min_levels of its levels must match one of the strategy's patterns. The first matching strategy wins.
_types_note: Provider type tags (app/external/work_type.py) grouped into classes. A tag in no class makes an identified work 'other': it counts neither as a major reference nor as an internet site.
_confirmed_note: Only a lookup whose identity was confirmed says what the entry is.
_web_note: An entry no catalogue identified, that gives a web address and says it was retrieved or accessed online, is counted as an internet site.
_text_types_note: An entry no catalogue confirmed is typed from its own citation text, in this order; the first class with a matching pattern wins. Repository and preprint entries count neither as major references nor as internet sites. A wrong 'major' only keeps the counts from lowering a grade, so the journal, conference and book cues may be broad; the web typing is the one that can lower a grade, so it is kept narrow. An entry no rule types stays unidentified.
_isbn_note: An unconfirmed entry whose parsed record carries an ISBN, and no repository cue, is a book.
_web_scholarly_note: Web typing needs a web cue and an address in the entry, and none of these scholarly cues: an entry retrieved from a publisher or DOI address may be a journal article, so it stays unidentified.
_quality_quantifiers_note: What a quality level's own words say about the share of the list that is journal or conference papers or books (database-confirmed or typed from the citation text). Each pattern must be about reliable or peer-reviewed sources and must not match its own negation. A level is decided only when its share holds however the unconfirmed entries turn out AND every other level's share is ruled out (min_share: ruled out when the highest possible share is at or below it; max_share: when the lowest possible share is at or above it). A level whose words match none of these cannot be checked against the counts, so no level is decided.
_wording_note: Every sentence this step writes on a criterion row. {placeholders} are filled from the counts. Counts are written as labelled numbers so no sentence depends on a plural. Entries typed from citation text as web pages are only ever information: they may be journal articles retrieved online, so they never decide a level.

wording.counts: Reference list: {entries} entries. Journal or conference papers or books: {major}{from_text}. Web sources: {web}.{repositories}{other} Type not known: {unclassified}.
wording.counts_from_text: ({n} classified from how the entry is written)
wording.counts_lookup_unavailable: Not yet looked up because a scholarly database could not be reached: {n} (a later check may identify them).
wording.web_note: Entries that look like web pages: {web}. Every level of this format allows no more than {limit} internet sites. Decide whether these entries count as internet sites under this format, then choose a grade.
wording.inventory_short: Even if every unconfirmed entry were a journal or conference paper or book, the list would have at most {best_major} major references, and the lowest level, {lowest}, needs {needed}. No level fits, so VERIDICAL did not choose one. Please check the reference list.
wording.inventory_open: Only entries confirmed in a scholarly database (such as Crossref or OpenAlex) can lower this grade. Unconfirmed entries: {uncertain}. Depending on what they turn out to be, the counts allow anything from {low} up to {high}. The counts also cannot show formatting errors, so VERIDICAL did not choose a level.
wording.inventory_ungraded: The counts allow {level}, but the formatting part of this criterion was not graded automatically, so VERIDICAL did not choose a level. Please check the reference list.
wording.inventory_lowered: The AI graded the formatting {grader}. The counts of major references and internet sites allow no higher than {level}, so the grade was lowered to {level}.
wording.inventory_same: The AI graded the formatting {level}, and the counts allow this level.
wording.inventory_formatting: The counts allow up to {count_level}; the AI's formatting grade, {level}, sets this one.
wording.quality_none: No level's wording fits this share of journal or conference papers or books, so VERIDICAL did not choose one. Please check the reference list.
wording.quality_several: These counts fit more than one level ({levels}); what separates them is not something the counts show, so VERIDICAL did not choose a level. Please check the reference list.
wording.quality_decided: Only this level's share of journal or conference papers or books fits these counts, however the unconfirmed entries turn out. The counts do not check the rest of the level's wording.
wording.no_entries: No reference entries were available to count.
wording.problem_not_finished: The citation check did not finish, so the reference list could not be counted. Please grade this criterion from the reference list yourself.
wording.problem_selection: VERIDICAL could not reliably tell where each reference entry starts and ends, so it did not count them. Please grade this criterion from the reference list yourself.
wording.problem_empty: No reference list was found to count. Please check the manuscript.
wording.problem_unread_pages: Some pages could not be read ({pages}), so the reference list may be incomplete and was not counted. Please check the reference list.
wording.problem_boundary: VERIDICAL could not confirm where the reference list starts and ends, so it was not counted. Please check the reference list.
wording.problem_partial: The citation check could not read the whole reference list, so it was not counted. Please check the reference list.
wording.entries_to_check: Entries to check, by their place in the reference list: {groups}.
wording.quality_share: Entries that can be journal or conference papers or books: {share} of {entries}.
wording.quality_unverifiable: Some levels of this format describe sources in words the counts cannot check, so no level can be shown to be the only one that fits, and VERIDICAL did not choose one. Please check the reference list.
wording.quality_open: Depending on what the unconfirmed entries turn out to be, this share could fit {levels}, so VERIDICAL did not choose a level. Please check the reference list.
wording.problem_unreadable: VERIDICAL could not read the manuscript's text in a reliable order, so the reference list could not be counted. Please grade this criterion from the reference list yourself.

_partial_list_note: Coverage reasons from the citation check that mean entries may be missing from the list, so it is not counted. Other reasons (body pages, claim checks, single lookups) leave the entries counted as unconfirmed.
